messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: PROD inference pool 'inference-prod-ptp' reporting repeated NCCL communicator timeouts — severity: page. Affected: multi-GPU tensor/pipeline parallel jobs. See /incidents/1976551234 for context.
oncall-bot: Incident runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nccl_collectives — please ack and follow handoff procedure.
maya: acked. I'm oncall for PG-Infra. hopping on the call.
chris: oncall-ml here. Observing elevated 5xxs for a subset of requests that hit pipeline-parallel models. Some pods restarting.
linh: i'm seeing a bunch of `CUDA_ERROR_DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and `NCCL WARN` in the agent logs. copied tail of a failing pod:```
E cuda: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E nccl: unhandled cuda error from transport 0
E nccl: comm destroy called after timeout
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runtime/worker.py", line 402, in step
    comm.allreduce(tensor)
RuntimeError: NCCL_COMMUNICATION_ERROR
```
aisha: good catches. is this correlated to a scheduled rollout?
maya: nope, there was a small infra scaling event ~17:02 where we added 4 nodes to the pool due to autoscale. no recent model pushes.
david: customer impact assessment: internal dashboards show latency spike and 15% error rate for model: gpt-4b-ptp-v2 in us-west1 for ~7 minutes. A few enterprise customers reported degraded inference.
chris: hypothesis: some nodes experienced GPU driver flakiness causing NCCL communicator teardown. We also see mixed GPU types on the same job after autoscale — possible topology mismatch + nvlink fallback triggered.
maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon/drain affected nodes 2) restart failing pods with `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` and `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` 3) fallback: re-route new requests to single-GPU sharded variant (gpt-4b-sharded) until health restored.
linh: running `kubectl get pods -o wide | grep inference-prod-ptp | grep CrashLoop` shows 6 pods on nodes gke-prod-ptp-3 and gke-prod-ptp-7. draining gke-prod-ptp-3 now.
ops-bot: @maya initiated node drain gke-prod-ptp-3. ETA for pod eviction ~120s.
maya: executed `gcloud compute ssh node/gke-prod-ptp-7 -- bash -lc "sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver | tail -n 200"` — driver logs show repeated timeouts to the GPU on that node. suspect hardware or driver crash.
aisha: moving traffic now: setting routing policy to prefer us-west1-dedicated cluster for model gpt-4b-ptp-v2. Patch applied, rerouting in progress.
david: notifying account owners for impacted customers: cc @support-team.
chris: while draining, i'm also patching deployment env to include `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` and bumping `NCCL_TIMEOUT=300`. will rollout canary 10% first.
linh: canary logs after env set: ```
NCCL INFO: Async error handling enabled
NCCL INFO: Rendezvous OK for rank 0..3
WARNING: Reduced bandwidth on link nvlink-1
```
maya: good sign. if canary looks stable for 2 minutes we'll increase to 50%.
ops-bot: drain complete for gke-prod-ptp-3, pods rescheduled to other nodes.
chris: canary -> 50% now. watching metrics.
aisha: we still see 2 pods failing on gke-prod-ptp-7. rebooting node via cloud console.
maya: reboot initiated. also adding a temporary guard in the routing layer to avoid scheduling PTP jobs on nodes with mixed GPU models.
david: customer comms: "We're investigating an intermittent multi-GPU communication issue affecting some production inference; we've routed traffic to alternate capacity and are mitigating. We'll update in 30m."
linh: after reboot, node came up healthy but `nvidia-smi` shows ECC errors on GPU0. marking gke-prod-ptp-7 for hardware replacement.
chris: post-mitigation: error rate down to baseline, latency recovered. we should keep `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` as default for a day and monitor.
maya: handoff to next oncall in 20m. next oncall: @chris (ML), @linh (infra). please take over postmortem and followup actions: replace GPU on gke-prod-ptp-7, add scheduling rule to prevent mixed-gpu ptp placements, and add a runbook note to check driver versions after autoscale events.
ops-bot: @chris acknowledged the handoff.
chris: ack. I'll start a postmortem doc and list action items. thanks all. :thumbsup:
